channel.title: Eldar Brothers Studios Blog
channel.description: Series, visual styles and what to watch next, from Eldar Brothers Studios

item.title: Animated comics: motion comics and cartoon adaptations
item.description: Animated comics are either motion comics, where real comic panels get voices, music and light movement, or cartoons redrawn from a comic. Examples and history.

item.title: What is stop motion? How it works, history and films
item.description: Stop motion is animation made by moving real objects a little between photographs. How it works, how to spot it, its history and the best-known films.

item.title: What is a plot twist? Meaning, types and examples
item.description: A plot twist is a sudden turn that changes a story's direction or what you thought you knew. Types of twists, famous movie examples and why spoilers hurt less.

item.title: What is anime? Meaning, history and where to start
item.description: Anime is animation made in Japan. Where the word comes from, how to recognize the style, key dates from 1917 to Spirited Away, and which shows to start with.

item.title: What is a limited series? Meaning, Emmys and examples
item.description: A limited series tells one complete story in a set number of episodes and is not meant to return. How it differs from a miniseries and an anthology series.

item.title: What is pixel art? Meaning, style and where it is used
item.description: Pixel art is digital art built pixel by pixel on a small grid with few colors. How to recognize it, where it came from, and what it is used for today.

item.title: What is Art Deco? The style, its look and its history
item.description: Art Deco is the sleek geometric design style of the 1920s and 1930s, named after a 1925 Paris exhibition. How to spot it and where it shows up on screen.

item.title: What is pop art? The movement, its look and artists
item.description: Pop art is the 1950s–60s movement that turned comics, adverts, soup cans and film stars into art. Where it started, how to spot it and how it reached TV.

item.title: What is abstract art? Meaning in simple words
item.description: Abstract art shows no recognizable things, only shape, color, line and mark. Where it came from, who made the first abstract works and how to look at it.

item.title: What is creepypasta? Meaning, origins and famous stories
item.description: Creepypasta is horror fiction born and shared online. What the word means, how it grew from 4chan, and the famous stories, from Slender Man to the Backrooms.

item.title: Liminal space: meaning, the Backrooms and films
item.description: A liminal space is an in-between place, like an empty hallway or a mall after hours. What the term means, the internet aesthetic, the Backrooms and films.

item.title: What is cyberpunk? The genre, its origins and key films
item.description: Cyberpunk is science fiction about high tech and low life: hackers, megacorporations and neon cities. Where it came from, the key books and films, and the look.

item.title: Art styles: a list of names and how to spot each one
item.description: A list of 22 major art styles, from the Renaissance to street art, with dates and one plain line on how to recognize each one and where they show up on screen.

item.title: Types of animation: the main techniques with examples
item.description: The main types of animation are hand-drawn, computer (3D), stop motion, cutout and pixel art. How each is made, famous examples, and how to tell them apart.

item.title: What is a web series? Meaning, length and examples
item.description: A web series is a run of short episodes, scripted or unscripted, made for the internet. How long episodes run, how it differs from TV, and famous examples.

item.title: Would you want to know when you die? What people say
item.description: Most people say no. In a study of over 2,000 adults, 86 to 90 percent did not want to know bad news ahead. What surveys found and how films play with the idea.
